title: A Noise-Invariant Determinism Theorem for Multi-Base Post-Processing in Shor's Order Finding (v0.5.0: nonstabilizerness / magic across quantum speedups)
description: v0.5.0 of the multi-base post-processing analysis of Shor's order finding, adding a new research direction: nonstabilizerness ("magic") across quantum speedups, measured and proven on the repository's numpy statevector simulation. RETAINED (unchanged): the six theorems on classical post-processing of multi-base order-finding measurements — (T1) noise-invariant determinism, (T2) logarithmic coverage time, (T3) exact noise scaling 1/g_M(eta), (T4) conditional compatibility with Regev's 2023 multi-base framework, (T5) a hybrid (C)+Regev b-trick factoring algorithm, and (T6) a sign-agnostic stochastic-resonance no-go — together with the closed-form sigma-curve p(sigma)=rho+(p0-rho)exp(-sigma^2) verified across five algorithm classes. NEW IN v0.5.0 (magic): using a verified stabilizer 2-Renyi entropy (SRE) tool computed by the XOR fast Walsh-Hadamard transform (cross-checked against three independent implementations to 1e-15), the work shows that the amount and density of nonstabilizerness separates the TYPE of quantum speedup. Main results: (i) Grover's unstructured-search state has magic that peaks at EXACTLY 3 bits as a function of problem size n and returns to zero at the answer, so its magic density M2/n -> 0 (closed form for a single marked item; peak = max of -log2(a^8+(1-a^2)^4) at a^2=1/2); (ii) the function graph state (1/sqrt N) sum_x |x>|f(x)> has M2 = 0 if and only if f is F2-affine, so Simon's algorithm with a linear (Clifford) oracle generates zero magic despite an exponential query speedup, while Shor's modular-exponentiation oracle is nonlinear and forces magic — formalizing how an oracle or FFT black box can HIDE the nonlinearity that is magic's true source; (iii) Shor's post-measurement comb state has magic growing with problem size, completing a speedup ladder: Clifford/affine -> 0, Grover (quadratic) -> bounded with density 0, Shor (exponential) -> growing toward maximal. A flat-state lemma (M2=0 iff the support is an F2-affine subspace) underpins the corollaries. Includes a reproducible 42-assertion proposition checker and a prior-art survey relating the results to arXiv:2605.05347 (Shor magic, preprint), published quantum-walk magic (Phys. Rev. Research 10.1103/7rwg-lhpv; Phys. Rev. B 113 075142, 10.1103/nzrp-49mr), and algorithm-magic comparisons (arXiv:2505.17185, 2507.16543). numpy + Python standard library only; no quantum libraries required.
